reviews.title: Way too unpolished for how long it’s existed…
reviews.text:
Letting the developer know: your own tip jar doesn’t work. When I click, it asks if I want premium again. I’m glad I didn’t sink more money into this, though, as it is plainly an unfinished product. 

In the “relax” section, what I assume are meant to be categories to pick from for the sounds are all blank grey sausages with nothing to say. Just a thing missing in the UI in an app that’s apparently been operating and accepting money for years.

The widget I wanted also doesn’t work. Even the widget that does work doesn’t display some info correctly. 

A quality of life improvement I’d appreciate: being able to pin or favorite sounds I’d like to use often. You also can’t look through the same categories (a simple search function would do wonders period) within choosing a sound for your current pomodoro timer.

There’s a lot more little unpolished things here or there that aren’t as major, and therefore I won’t waste my time nitpicking, 

While I appreciate the option here to not have to pay a subscription for such a small fee in this economy (others ask for $99.99…), you’re also accepting money for something in which half the features are either barely functionable or just non existent.

I’m going to attempt getting a refund, I think.

reviews.title: Paid $1.99 to not be able to use pro features on Apple watch
reviews.text: What the tittle says, I didn’t want to spend $10 on an app before trying it. Since there’s no free trial I was more than happy to pay the $1.99 to try the product. Unfortunately it would seem that $1.99 doesn’t go toward being able to use the pro features on your Apple Watch. I tried to select a sound to listen with the timer on my watch, and was prompted to select the $10 lifetime subscription. It’s really not that much money, but I already paid to try these features. Such a shame I do like the interface and it was easy to use from my watch, but if I can’t select a track to listen from my watch it completely defeats the point of the app, I can do the same thing with Spotify and the timer app if I’m just going to be using my phone to play the music anyway.
